uncited: **Inputs:** $K$ input images $\{I_k\}_{k=1}^K$, camera poses for each view, and a target 3D point cloud or volume grid defined by spatial dimensions $H/8 \times W/8 \times D$.
**Windowed Color Vector:** For each 3D point, a $9 \times 9$ window is sampled from each of the $K$ feature maps centered at the 2D projection of the point.
Pass each input image $I_k$ through a weight-sharing 2D CNN.
The CNN consists of 6 residual blocks [12].
Every 2 residual blocks include a stride-2 convolutional layer to achieve 2× downsampling.
Feed the 1/8 resolution convolutional features into a joint multi-view Transformer.
This Transformer extends the 2-view cross-attention architecture (from GMFlow [34, 35]) to $K$ input views.
*   Project the 3D point to 2D coordinates in each of the $K$ input views.
*   Sample a $9 \times 9$ window centered at these 2D coordinates from the 1/8 resolution feature maps.
Quantify multi-view consistency by computing pair-wise cosine similarities between the sampled features $\{f_i\}_{i=1}^K$.
*   Normalize all feature vectors $f_i$ to unit length.
*   Collect them into a matrix $F \in \mathbb{R}^{K \times M}$.
The weights $w_i$ are normalized learned weights.
Concatenate the aggregated cosine similarity $\hat{s}$, the aggregated color $\hat{c}$, and the aggregated feature $\hat{f}$.
Project this concatenated vector to a $C$-dimensional vector using a linear layer.
**Time Complexity:** The computation of pair-wise cosine similarities is $O(K^2 \cdot M)$ per point, where $K$ is the number of views and $M$ is the feature dimension.
**Limitations:** Relies on the quality of the 2D CNN and Transformer features.
